title: App profile failover: disaster recovery, cloud unreachable, captive portals

prose.text: The app profile handles four different situations, and they should not be confused.

prose.label: The Zscaler cloud is down (disaster recovery).
prose.text: {{zia-dr-scope}} {{zia-dr-actions}} {{dr-activation}} {{zpa-dr-scope}} What disaster recovery is for, and how Private Access activates it, is in [[zpa.private-service-edges.disaster-recovery]].

prose.label: The disaster recovery PAC file.
prose.text: {{policy-based-access-lists}} {{private-access-allow}} {{private-bc-pac}} The sample PAC files scope their PROXY return by client version in two ways {{divergence:proxy-return-version}}. {{dns-txt-and-testing}} The linked DNS TXT record article is open {{gap:dns-txt-article}}.

prose.label: The cloud or the tunnel cannot be reached (failover).
prose.text: {{profile-failover-overrides-global}} {{profile-failover-options}} The tenant-wide App Fail Open settings these override are in [[zcc.forwarding-profiles.fail-open]].

prose.label: A captive portal is in the way.
The PAC file cannot be reached.

prose.text: How the disaster recovery block is spelled on the wire, where the sources disagree, is in [[zcc.api.web-policy-wire:dr-key-names]].

checks.do: Whether the outage is the Zscaler cloud (disaster recovery, activated by DNS TXT record) or reachability from this device (failover).
For failover, whether the app profile sets its own behavior or follows the global App Fail Open setting, and whether the client version honors the profile setting.

zia-dr-scope.statement: Disaster Recovery for Internet & SaaS gives users access while the Internet & SaaS service is down, and only to enrolled users.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: Disaster Recovery for Internet & SaaS provides users access even when the Internet & SaaS service is down and is available only to enrolled users.

zia-dr-actions.statement: When enabled, the profile chooses what happens during it: direct internet access bypassing the app, no internet access (all traffic dropped at the endpoint), policy-based access for web traffic allowing or blocking URLs through a custom PAC file, or, on Windows 4.8 and later, policy-based access on all ports, which also uses a custom PAC file and forwards the selected traffic over Z-Tunnel 2.0.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: Direct Internet Access: Traffic bypasses Zscaler Client Connector, giving the user access to all applications through direct internet access.
Disable Internet Access: All traffic is dropped at the endpoint and users do not have access to the internet.
Policy Based Access (Web only): You can either block or allow access to specific URLs using a custom PAC file.
Policy Based Access (All Ports): You can either block or allow access to specific URLs using a custom PAC file.
This option allows you to forward the selected internet traffic using Z-Tunnel 2.0.
Available only for Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later for Windows.

dr-activation.statement: Disaster recovery is activated or tested by updating a DNS TXT record value, and Activate Test Mode is for app profiles whose selected users or groups are part of a group that tests disaster recovery.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: Activation: Activate or test disaster recovery by updating the DNS TXT record value.
Test Mode: Enable Activate Test Mode if the selected users or groups for the app profile are part of a group to test disaster recovery.

zpa-dr-scope.statement: Disaster Recovery for Private Access gives users access to applications while the Private Access service is down, and is available only to enrolled users.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: Disaster Recovery for Private Access provides users access to applications when the Private Access service is down and is available only to enrolled users.

policy-based-access-lists.statement: Allow Zscaler Preselected Destinations (Recommended), when enabled, lets users access only the URLs present in the Zscaler-provided global database allowlist and blocks the rest. A custom PAC URL (with the http:// or https:// prefix) can be configured for destinations users can access when the Internet & SaaS service is down; configured together with the global database URL, both URL lists are allowed and the custom destinations URL takes precedence in any conflict, and traffic can also be forwarded to a proxy server. If both the Allow Zscaler Preselected Destinations and Custom Destinations fields are enabled, the return drop; syntax must be removed from the custom PAC file statement because it blocks the URLs in the global allowlist.

quotes: Allow Zscaler Preselected Destinations (Recommended): When enabled, users can access only the URLs that are present in the Zscaler-provided global database allowlist. The rest of the URLs are blocked.
You can configure a custom PAC URL (with the http:// or https:// prefix) that users can access when the Internet & SaaS service is down.

When configured in conjunction with the global database URL, both URL lists are allowed. The custom destinations URL takes precedence when there are any conflicts. You can also forward the traffic to a proxy server.

If you have enabled both the Allow Zscaler Preselected Destinations and Custom Destinations fields, ensure that you remove the return drop; syntax from the custom PAC file statement because it blocks the URLs listed in the Zscaler-provided global database allowlist.

private-access-allow.statement: When configuring the custom DR PAC file, access to the Private Access IP range 100.64.0.0/16 and the Private Access domains zpath.net and zpatwo.net must be allowed to prevent blocking Private Access traffic.

quotes: When configuring the custom PAC file, ensure that you allow access to the Private Access IP range 100.64.0.0/16 and Private Access domains, zpath.net and zpatwo.net, to prevent blocking Private Access traffic.

private-bc-pac.statement: For the private business continuity cloud, the Custom DR PAC URL must point to the private PAC server (https://<private pac domain>.pac.zsbcs.net/<insert the rest of the PAC URL>); as of the 2026-11-04 capture the page says the private business continuity feature is in limited availability. The PAC file can return PROXY to the Zscaler-managed business continuity subcloud to maintain policies in the business continuity environment.

quotes: You must configure the Custom DR PAC URL pointing to the private PAC server for the private business continuity cloud (https://<private pac domain>.pac.zsbcs.net/<insert the rest of the PAC URL>.
The private business continuity feature is in limited availability.
Return PROXY to the Zscaler-managed business continuity subcloud to maintain your policies in the business continuity environment.

dns-txt-and-testing.statement: An organization with Internet & SaaS only cannot download the DNS Record Generator. TXT Record Signing Public Key takes a valid public key uploaded with Upload, and only PEM files can be uploaded. Zscaler recommends that disaster recovery be tested periodically with just a few users.

quotes: If you have Internet & SaaS only, you cannot download the DNS Record Generator.
TXT Record Signing Public Key: Click Upload to add a valid public key. You can only upload PEM files.
Zscaler recommends that disaster recovery be tested periodically with just a few users.

profile-failover-overrides-global.statement: Failover settings on the app profile take precedence over the global App Fail Open settings, from Client Connector 4.6 for Windows and 4.8 for macOS.

quotes: If you use Zscaler Client Connector version 4.6 and later for Windows or Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later for macOS, you can set up failover settings on the app profile that take precedence over these settings.

If failover settings are also configured in Client Connector Support, these failover settings take precedence. This feature is available only in Zscaler Client Connector version 4.6 and later for Windows.

profile-failover-options.statement: For ZIA Cloud Not Reachable and for Z-Tunnel 1.0 failover, the profile can follow the global setting (the default), allow direct internet access, disable internet access (HTTP/HTTPS blocked, other traffic allowed), or fall back to the Internet & SaaS disaster recovery settings.

evidence.after: Win V4.7 and Older Client Configuration:
quotes: Follow Global Config: Allow access based on the setting in ZIA Cloud Not Reachable in Client Connector Support. This option is selected by default.
Direct Internet Access: Users are allowed to bypass the app and access the internet directly.
Disable Internet Access: Blocks HTTP/HTTPS traffic. All other traffic is allowed.
Fallback to ZIA DR: If Enable ZIA DR is enabled, follow the traffic forwarding settings in Disaster Recovery for Internet & SaaS.
Z-Tunnel Failover: Select one of the following options to set what happens if Zscaler Client Connector cannot establish a tunnel (Z-Tunnel 1.0 only):

cannot establish a tunnel (Z-Tunnel 1.0 only): - Follow Global Config: Allow access based on the setting in Z-Tunnel Failover in Client Connector Support. This option is selected by default. - Direct Internet Access: Users are allowed to bypass the app and access the internet directly.

Z-Tunnel Failover in Client Connector Support. This option is selected by default. - Direct Internet Access: Users are allowed to bypass the app and access the internet directly. - Disable Internet Access: Blocks HTTP/HTTPS traffic. All other traffic is allowed.

Disable Internet Access: Blocks HTTP/HTTPS traffic. All other traffic is allowed. - Fallback to ZIA DR: If Enable ZIA DR is enabled, follow the traffic forwarding settings in Disaster Recovery for Internet & SaaS. - Global Bypasses

captive-portal.statement: On Windows 4.5 and later the profile enables captive portal detection; with Fail Open on, the app keeps its services disabled for 1 to 60 minutes after detecting a captive portal and then re-enables them.

quotes: These settings apply only to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5 and later for Windows.
Enter the number of minutes the app must keep its services disabled after detecting a captive portal when Fail Open is enabled. You can enter any value between 1 and 60.
After the specified period, the app enables its services automatically and traffic is forwarded to the Zscaler service.

captive-portal-fail-open.statement: Fail Open enables a fail-open state when a captive portal is detected: with it enabled, the app blocks all traffic until the user registers in the captive portal using the embedded browser, which must first be enabled on the profile (Embedded Captive Portal).
captive-portal-fail-open.conditions: Added (verifier w2 A17); it contradicts the legacy reading of fail open as allowing direct traffic when the tunnel cannot be established. Narrowed per review: the page does not set this against opening traffic; its next field keeps the app's services disabled for a set period after a captive portal is detected when Fail Open is enabled (captive-portal).

quotes: Fail Open: Select to enable a fail-open state if a captive portal is detected. If enabled, Zscaler Client Connector blocks all traffic until users register in the captive portal using the embedded browser.
To use this feature, you must first enable Embedded Captive Portal in the app profile.
Embedded Captive Portal: Select to enable an embedded browser to use when Zscaler Client Connector detects a captive portal.

captive-portal-keys.statement: By name, these settings are the web policy keys `enableCaptivePortalDetection`, `enableFailOpen` and `captivePortalWebSecDisableMinutes`, which the Go SDK sends on the web policy body.
captive-portal-keys.conditions: The key-to-setting mapping is by name; no source states it. The API document has these keys only on the fail-open policy, not on the web policy edit body.

quotes: `json:"enableCaptivePortalDetection"`
`json:"enableFailOpen"`
`json:"captivePortalWebSecDisableMinutes"`

allow-unreachable-pac.statement: The Python SDK documents `allowUnreachablePac` as whether traffic is allowed when the PAC file is unreachable; the Go SDK calls it a legacy flag that the API still echoes on reads though the admin UI no longer renders it.

quotes: allow_unreachable_pac (bool): Whether traffic is allowed when the PAC file is unreachable.
AllowUnreachablePac is the legacy flag the provider has surfaced
the API echoes it on reads even when
the UI no longer renders it. omitempty keeps it off the wire when
